title: A Prospective, Comparative, Clinical Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of Two Different 0.1% Riboflavin Solutions Used in Collagen Crosslinking Treatment for Patients with Keratoconus

license.statement: CC BY-NC 3.0 (article <license>; Dove Medical Press terms incorporating Creative Commons Attribution - Non Commercial unported v3.0)

groups.description: Flavin isotonic 0.1% riboflavin ophthalmic solution with 20% dextran (Biotech Ophthalmics), the new formulation the trial evaluates; epithelium-off Dresden CXL (central 8-10 mm debridement, riboflavin every 2 min for 30 min soaking, UVA 370 nm 3 mW/cm2 for 30 min, 5.4 J/cm2) for progressive keratoconus; randomized by computer-generated method; no cataract or other surgery in the described session

Peschke D 0.1% riboflavin with 20% dextran (PESCHKE Trade), the established comparator solution; epithelium-off Dresden CXL (central 8-10 mm debridement, riboflavin every 2 min for 30 min soaking, UVA 370 nm 3 mW/cm2 for 30 min, 5.4 J/cm2) for progressive keratoconus; randomized by computer-generated method; no cataract or other surgery in the described session

series.notes: mean ± SD; unit logMAR from the Table 3 row label; CDVA = corrected distance visual acuity (footnote); n 50 from Tables 1-2 headers; per-visit n not reported
mean ± SD; unit logMAR from the Table 4 row label; CDVA = corrected distance visual acuity (footnote); n 50 from Tables 1-2 headers; per-visit n not reported

exclusions.what: Preoperative CDVA per group (Table 1 R7) and 12-month CDVA per group (Table 2 R6)
exclusions.reason: the same groups and visits are tabulated in Tables 3-4 with the full series; Tables 3-4 are cited instead

exclusions.what: Proportions reaching Snellen 20/40 or 20/200 and lines of CDVA gained or lost (Figures 3-4)

notes: 100 eyes of 61 patients (some patients contribute both eyes), 50 eyes per group.

Role: the article states that the trial evaluates the new Flavin formulation against the Peschke D solution that 'has been evaluated earlier in clinical trials and in market for a long time', so Flavin is treated and Peschke D control.
Visits on day 1 and at 2 weeks were performed but are not tabulated.
The study was supported by a grant from Biotech Vision Care and two authors are its consultants (Disclosure).
Inclusion required willingness to attend all follow-up visits (a preoperative criterion); one eye had sterile infiltrates that resolved (Discussion).

Tables 1-5 also tabulate sphere, cylinder, spherical equivalent, uncorrected acuity (logMAR), endothelial cell density, thinnest pachymetry, keratometry and demarcation line depth; none of these is used.
